title: implement wrap_forward_fn

atoms.evidence: def wrap_forward_fn(numpy_func: Callable, is_differentiable=True) -> Callable: → returns tensor_func closure — the single most-leveraged factory in part 4, generalizing 0_4_5/0_4_6
arg_arrays = tuple([(a.array if isinstance(a, Tensor) else a) for a in args]) — explicit unbox map over variadic *args
out_arr = numpy_func(*arg_arrays, **kwargs); out = Tensor(out_arr, requires_grad); if requires_grad: out.recipe = Recipe(...) — full box-and-attach

requires_grad = grad_tracking_enabled and is_differentiable and any([(isinstance(a, Tensor) and a.requires_grad) for a in args]) — now with all THREE gates (global toggle AND is_differentiable AND any-input-requires-grad)
First conjunct of the requires_grad expression; help dropdown explicitly enumerates 'Grad tracking is enabled' as one of three conditions
parents = {idx: a for idx, a in enumerate(args) if isinstance(a, Tensor)} — same dict-by-idx-with-Tensor-filter pattern as 0_4_6, now in the generic factory
out.recipe = Recipe(numpy_func, arg_arrays, kwargs, parents) — full 4-tuple constructed inside the generic wrapper
out = Tensor(out_arr, requires_grad) — the wrapper class instantiated inside the factory
is_differentiable parameter on wrap_forward_fn; used as eq = wrap_forward_fn(np.equal, is_differentiable=False); when False, requires_grad short-circuits to False so no Recipe is built

out_arr = numpy_func(*arg_arrays, **kwargs) AND Recipe(numpy_func, arg_arrays, kwargs, parents) — kwargs threaded into both the forward call AND the Recipe; help dropdown: 'kwargs should be used in two ways: once when actually calling numpy_func, and once when defining the Recipe object'; tested via _sum (dim, keepdim)
eq = wrap_forward_fn(np.equal, is_differentiable=False) — non-differentiable op registered via same factory with the flag
Cell wraps log/multiply/eq/sum but defers add_back_func calls (this exercise only tests the wrap side; registration shown but BACK_FUNCS calls happen in subsequent exercises 0_4_10+)

notes: 12 atoms — well above seed prediction of 11. The densest single exercise in §5 (the dispatcher cluster); composes every wrap_forward_fn atom plus is_differentiable_flag and non-diff-fn-wrap (via the eq example). The 2nd most conceptually important exercise per the markdown.
